To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have described a unique population with a specific diet and health profile and identified dietary patterns that are characteristic of the population, which are associated with cardiovascular risk factors.
the MANOLIS cohort is an elderly population that displays a high prevalence of overweight/obesity with an unhealthy diet and a high prevalence of cardiometabolic risk factors.

we recruited a population-based cohort of elderly people from the isolated Mylopotamou area in Crete, which has interesting characteristics in terms diet and health, and identified four dietary patterns that are characteristic of the population.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the relationship of dietary patterns with health and lifestyle parameters in the elderly population of the MANOLOS study.
the identification and characterization of the specific population of Mylopotamos, Crete, through the recruitment of a cohort and the collection of a wide array of data on diet, lifestyle and health.
the identification of a population that is unique in terms of diet, health and lifestyle.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the MANOLIS population is a healthy population in terms of diet, lifestyle, health and disease.
the MANOLIS study is an ideal setting to investigate the role of dietary habits on cardiometabolic risk factors and their relationship with the Mediterranean diet in the elderly.
the Cretan diet is not a single entity but a combination of different dietary patterns, with different associations with health outcomes, and that this is an area for further research.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Cretan diet, which is a Mediterranean dietary pattern, is associated with lower cardiovascular risk.
a healthy diet is associated with a healthy lifestyle and vice versa, while the Mediterranean diet, as a whole, is not a panacea.
the population-based cohort MANOLIS, with its unique dietary patterns and high cardiovascular risk, could be an ideal setting to test the effect of lifestyle interventions on health and ageing.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the population is at risk for cardiovascular disease.
the Cretan dietary pattern is not the same as the Mediterranean one.
a Mediterranean-like diet is associated with a healthy lifestyle and a lower burden of cardiometabolic risk factors.
